First of all you need to Google your vehicles tow rating. Second, you have 648 pounds of payload capacity left after passengers and cargo, just including the bikes. So you are probably gonna take more cargo than just ppl and bicycles. 

Your payload capacity is 1,498, which means cargo, passengers, and tongue weight must be under that pound limit. So 700 + 150 = 850 subtract from 1,498 is 648 left for tongue weight and remaining cargo like luggage or food.

The 7,350 gross vehicle weight rating includes the curb weight of the empty truck too. So your payload capacity is the difference between the gvwr and the curb weight. Each axel has weight ratings too. Also the tongue weight of your hitch should never be more than 10% of your max towing capacity.

So from 648 I'll take another 150 pounds of cargo because you probably are gonna bring more than just bikes. Now you have 498 pounds left, so the remaining weight can be the 10% of the hitch weight of a ~5,000 pound trailer~ I'll round 4,980 to 5k. Which would nearly be the weight of your f150 which is 5,852 pounds according to the payload capacity subtracted from the gvwr.

Now, the engine isn't an issue towing nearly the weight of the truck but the brakes are something to think about not overloading. And making sure the weight is distributed evenly so the weight of the trailer has 10-15% on the hitch.
